commands.description: Shows xLimbo's version, and holds its admin subcommands.

subcommands.description: Shows xLimbo's version, and who's in limbo.
Lists who's in limbo, and their place in line.
Sends a player into limbo on this server.
Sends a player back, or everyone with all: through the queue while it's on.

arguments.name: player
arguments.description: The player to send back, or all.

subcommands.description: Reloads config.yml and the language files, and applies them.
Checks the database, dependencies and platform, then prints a paste link for support.
Deletes everything kept about one player.

arguments.name: player
arguments.description: The player whose data is deleted, online or not.

commands.description: Go back to the main server.

permissions.description: See who's in limbo and their place in line: /xlimbo list.
Send a player into limbo on this server: /xlimbo send <player>.
Send a player, or everyone, back: /xlimbo back <player|all>.
Every admin subcommand of xLimbo, and its update notices.
Hear about newer versions of xLimbo when joining.

header: xLimbo: never drop a player again.
Apply changes with /xlimbo reload. Everything applies, even the world's name and
floor. A bad value falls back to its default with a warning in the console; xLimbo
never stops over config. The messages are in lang/: one file per language.

comment: How this plugin's messages look, and the language they're in. shared uses the
setting in plugins/Xena/config.yml, which every Xena plugin reads; anything else is
this plugin's own.
The language players see messages in: auto for each player's own (their client's
language setting), or one language for everyone, such as de or pt-BR.
The language of the console, and of players whose language has no file in lang/.
The look every message shares, used in messages as tags: <prefix>, <highlight>,
<success> and <error>. Colours are names (gray, gold) or hex (#B48CFF), with bold,
italic, underlined, strikethrough or obfuscated if you like: <#B48CFF><bold>.
<prefix> starts the default messages. Make it your server's name, such as
"<dark_gray>[<gradient:#B48CFF:#5EE08A>MyServer</gradient>]</dark_gray> ", or blank for none.
The colour of message text that has no tag of its own.
<highlight>: names and values, such as a player or a speed.
<success>: something turned on or done.
<error>: something refused or turned off.
The void world players wait in: one floor layer, nothing else. Changing its name,
floor-block or floor-y rebuilds it on /xlimbo reload; players are moved out and back.
The limbo world, created on startup. To use the server's main world instead, set
this to its name (level-name in server.properties) and give it xLimbo's generator
in bukkit.yml (worlds: <name>: generator: xLimbo).
The one-block-thick floor everyone stands on: a block as Minecraft names it, such as
white_stained_glass. It must be solid and not fall.
The floor's height. Players stand one block above it.
false keeps the world off disk: it starts fresh every time the server does. true
saves it, for builds that should last.
Start fresh on every startup even when auto-save is on.
The world border's width in blocks. It caps how much world can ever exist.
Arriving players land up to this many blocks from the centre, so they don't stack.
Small keeps a mass arrival to a handful of chunks; the land around it is kept ready.
Chunks sent to players in this world, 2 to 32. -1 keeps the server's setting.
Chunks that tick around players in this world, 2 to 32. -1 keeps the server's setting.
What arriving players get.
Put arriving players in creative.
Give arriving players flight, and keep it on.
Players can't see each other. With hundreds arriving at once, everyone tracking
everyone else is the biggest load a limbo has; this takes it away.
Arriving. The welcome message is join.welcome in lang/.
Hide the "joined the game" broadcast.
Clear the arriving player's chat first.
Hide the "left the game" broadcast.
Hide death messages.
The server /join and automatic returns send players to: its name in your proxy's
config, such as "main". Only with send-back.via: proxy.
How players go back. proxy: xLimbo is your network's fallback server, and players go
to main-server through the proxy (BungeeCord, Waterfall or Velocity). teleport: xLimbo
is a world on this server (/xlimbo send puts players in it), and players go back with
a teleport, through xTeleport when it's installed.
With via: teleport, where to: previous (where they were before limbo, or spawn if
that isn't known), spawn (xTeleport's /spawn, or the main world's), warp:<name>
(an xTeleport warp), or the name of a destination another plugin gave xTeleport.
Send players back on their own this long after they arrive. The message they get is
auto-join.sending in lang/.
Only without server-check, which sends players back as soon as the main server is up.
How long after arriving.
Watch the main server, and send everyone back as soon as it's up, instead of waiting
for /join or auto-join. Only with send-back.via: proxy. Everyone here is told
(server-check.up in lang/) when it comes back.
Your main server's address as xLimbo can reach it (not the proxy's), such as
"127.0.0.1:25566". xLimbo asks it for its status, as a server list does.
How automatic returns are paced. While a player waits their turn, their action bar
shows queue.action-bar from lang/ (blank shows the normal one instead).
How many players are sent back each second, so the main server isn't flooded the
moment it's back. 0 sends everyone at once.
/join: sends you back. Everyone has it by default. Its messages are join-command.* in lang/.
Blank ("") lets anyone.
Seconds between uses, per player, so nobody can spam your proxy.
A hint repeated on every player's action bar: action-bar.hint in lang/.
Ticks between updates (20 is one second).
Players here are in creative, so these stop them breaking, lagging or escaping the
server. Each can be turned off; one that's off costs nothing.
The floor can't be broken, pushed, or built under.
Put players who fall below threshold-y back on the floor.
No void or fall damage, so a rescue never becomes a death loop.
Nether and End portals, and Eyes of Ender in End portal frames.
Placing water and lava, and liquids flowing.
Sand, gravel, anvils, concrete powder and other blocks that fall.
Fire spreading, burning and being lit.
Every explosion.
Mobs spawning.
Redstone, pistons and dispensers.
Dropped items.
Armour stands, boats, minecarts, item frames, paintings, End crystals and spawn eggs.
Removes stray entities this often: everything but players and what builds are made of
(armour stands, item frames, paintings, displays, interactions, markers), and anything
tagged xlimbo.keep. 0 turns it off.
Limits how fast each player can place blocks, against lag machines.
Telling you when a newer version is out: in the console, and to players with
<plugin>.admin.update when they join. Asks Modrinth once a day, off the server's threads,
sending only the plugin's version, the platform and the Minecraft version.
Whether to ask at all.
Which releases to hear of: release, beta (betas and releases) or alpha (everything).
Under a long list in chat (/homes, /history, ...) when it has more than one page.
<previous> and <next> are the list's command for those pages; what's inside
<has_previous>...</has_previous> or <has_next>...</has_next> shows only when there's such a page.
In the console, and to players with <plugin>.admin.update as they join, when a newer version is out
on the update channel the config picks. <url> is its download page.
/<plugin> debug, before the health checks' results.
/<plugin> debug: the database answered. <database> is where it is, such as "MySQL at db:3306/minecraft".
/<plugin> debug: the database didn't answer. <reason> is the driver's, in English.
/<plugin> debug: every plugin or mod it depends on is there. <names> lists them, or says none.

messages.english: <gold>!</gold> Dependencies: <names> not installed, so what needs them is off.
comment: /<plugin> debug: optional plugins or mods that aren't installed.
/<plugin> debug: plugins or mods it needs that aren't installed.

messages.english: <success>✔</success> Threads: tasks run where they should (<threading>).
comment: /<plugin> debug: a task on the global thread and one off it each ran where it should.
<threading> is how the server runs work, in English: "Folia's regions", "one main thread".
/<plugin> debug: a task ran on the wrong thread, or didn't run. <reason> is in English.
/<plugin> debug: the config and language files had nothing wrong when they were last read.
/<plugin> debug: problems found the last time the files were read; the console and the report have them all.
/<plugin> debug: every module the config turns on is running.
/<plugin> debug: modules that failed. The report says why.
/<plugin> debug: a check that didn't finish. <check> is its name and <reason> why, in English.

messages.english: <prefix>Debug report: <click:open_url:'<url>'><hover:show_text:'Open it'><highlight><url></highlight></hover></click>. Share this link when asking for help; passwords and tokens are removed.
comment: /<plugin> debug: the report's link at a paste service (mclo.gs).

messages.english: <prefix>Couldn't upload the debug report (<reason>), so it's in <highlight><file></highlight> in the plugin's folder.
comment: /<plugin> debug: the upload failed, so the report was written to a file. <reason> is in English.

messages.english: <prefix>Debug report saved as <highlight><file></highlight> in the plugin's folder.
comment: /<plugin> debug, when uploading is turned off.
/<plugin> debug: the report couldn't be uploaded or written. <reason> is in English.
/<plugin> import: the other plugin's files or tables weren't found.

messages.english: <prefix><error>An import is already running; wait for it to finish.</error>
comment: /<plugin> import while one is running.

messages.english: <prefix>Dry run from <source>: <highlight><importable></highlight> of <total> records would be imported, <skipped> skipped. Nothing was changed.
comment: /<plugin> import <source> --dry-run: what a real run would do.
/<plugin> import: the run starts.

messages.english: <prefix>Carrying on the import from <source> where it stopped, after <done> of <total> records...
comment: /<plugin> import: a run that stopped before is carried on.
/<plugin> import: progress, every few seconds.
/<plugin> import: one record that failed. The import carries on; the console lists them all.
/<plugin> import: the run finished.

messages.english: <prefix><error>The import from <source> stopped: <reason></error> Run it again to carry on where it left off.
comment: /<plugin> import: the run stopped, such as when the other plugin's database went away. <reason> is in English.
/<plugin> migrate to the storage type in use.

messages.english: <prefix><error>A migration is already running; wait for it to finish.</error>
comment: /<plugin> migrate while one is running.

messages.english: <prefix><error>The <type> database already has data (<tables>).</error> Add --force to replace it with this server's.
comment: /<plugin> migrate: the target isn't empty. <tables> lists its tables with their rows.
/<plugin> migrate: the copy starts.
/<plugin> migrate: one table is copied.

messages.english: <prefix><success>Moved the data to <type> and checked it (rows: <rows>).</success> The plugin now uses <type>.
comment: /<plugin> migrate: done; the config's storage type was changed and applied.

messages.english: <prefix><error>Moving the data to <type> failed: <reason></error> The plugin still uses <from>.
comment: /<plugin> migrate: it failed, and the storage type wasn't changed. <reason> is in English.
/<plugin> forget: the name isn't one the server knows. A UUID works too.
/<plugin> forget: done.

messages.english: <prefix><error>Some of <player>'s data couldn't be deleted (<failed>).</error> Records deleted: <records>. Run it again.
comment: /<plugin> forget: part of it failed. <failed> lists what, with why, in English.
/<plugin> reload: config.yml and the language files were read again and applied.
What's inside <has_one>...</has_one> shows when one module is on, <has_many>...</has_many> otherwise.
/<plugin> reload: one line per problem found in the files, in English. The console has them too.
/<plugin> reload: a module that failed, and why, in English.

messages.english: <prefix><error>Reloading <plugin> failed; the console has the details.
comment: /<plugin> reload: something went wrong; the settings from before are still in use.
Rare: a command that went away as it was typed.

messages.english: <prefix><error>You don't have permission to do that.
comment: The sender lacks the command's permission.
The console or a command block ran a command only players can use.
The command was typed with missing or extra words. <usage> is how to type it.
No player the sender can see is online by the name typed (<player>).
A number was expected. <input> is what was typed.
A whole number was expected. <input> is what was typed.
A number below the least the command takes (<min>).
A number above the most the command takes (<max>).
A word that isn't one of those the command takes (<choices>, comma-separated).
What was typed can't be used: true or false, a length of time, a name. <reason> is in English.
The command has a cooldown. <time> is how long is left.
A command that needs confirming, such as forget. <line> is the command, <time> how long there is.

messages.english: <prefix><error>Something went wrong running that command; the console has the details.
comment: The command hit an error. The console has what happened.

messages.english: <prefix>xLimbo <highlight><version></highlight> on <platform>: <count> in limbo, <waiting> waiting to go back. <gray>/xlimbo reload | debug | list | send | back | forget
comment: /xlimbo on its own.

messages.english: <prefix>The server is unavailable right now, so you're waiting here. Type <highlight>/join</highlight> to go back.
comment: Sent to a player when they arrive (2.x's join.custom-join-message). Blank for none.

messages.english: <prefix>You're in limbo for now. Type <highlight>/join</highlight> to go back.
comment: Sent to a player sent into limbo on this server (/xlimbo send, the API, xTeleport). Blank for none.
/join, as the player goes. <server> is main-server, or the teleport's destination.
/join used again too soon. <seconds> is the whole seconds left.
/join from outside limbo, with send-back.via: teleport.
Sent as a player is sent back on their own (auto-join, server-check, the queue). Blank for none.

messages.english: <prefix><success>The server is back up!</success> Sending everyone back...
comment: To everyone here when server-check sees the main server come back up. Blank for none.
The action bar while a player waits their turn. Blank shows the hint instead. Vanished players aren't counted.

messages.english: <white>Type <highlight><bold>/join</bold></highlight> to go back to the server
comment: Repeated on every player's action bar (action-bar.enabled).

messages.english: <prefix><error>You couldn't be sent back just now.</error> Try <highlight>/join</highlight> again in a moment.
comment: With send-back.via: teleport, a teleport back that didn't happen (unsafe, or its destination is gone).
/xlimbo list, before the names. Vanished players are counted only for those who can see them.
/xlimbo send.

messages.english: <prefix><error><highlight><player></highlight> wasn't sent: another plugin stopped it, or the limbo world isn't ready.

comment: /xlimbo back <player>.
/xlimbo back all.

messages.english: <prefix><error><highlight><player></highlight> stays: a hold, another plugin, or the main server being down kept them.

events.description: A player on this server is about to be sent into limbo. Cancel it to keep them where they are.
A player arrived in limbo, with why as far as xLimbo can tell.
A player is about to be sent back. Cancel it to keep them in limbo.
A player was sent back, through the proxy or by a teleport.
Server-check saw the main server go up or down.
